documents.evidence: Arrival dates originally tell the weekly volunteer which owners to contact. The rewrite identifies whose work to ask about, leaving open whom the volunteer asks. It retains the handling note, accessible storage, paired lid, timely private damage report and named contact during an absence.

Both connect dated chair counts to booking capacity, a reachable keyholder to driver delays, and folded and stacked measurements to vehicle capacity. Both isolate and tag damaged chairs, leave time to inspect and clean returns before collection, and permit a substitute returner when an organizer leaves early.

Both keep names together and break lines for quick reading, show captions from the opening words, and use a full muted review to detect replies that lack context. Both identify the quoted writer when reading begins, title a looping interview for midstream arrivals, and capture title and playback time so staff can locate errors.

Both give beginners a whole-song fallback, let partners stay together, and teach them to resume after losing the beat. Both explain traffic on a crowded floor, move belongings out of dancers' paths, and make water visible and reachable so a newcomer can take a break independently.

Both reserve willing bakers' bread for after-work arrivals within the announced hours, provide bags and a pencil for identification at home, and use next-day serving tips to encourage unfamiliar choices. Both retain extra bread for empty-handed neighbors, a family drawing activity without touching samples, and contributors' advance choice of where leftovers go.

An unfinished early sketch encourages imperfect marks, scrap paper permits private practice, and a cardboard viewfinder narrows a border to a drawable area in both versions. Each also connects plant locations to finding specimens, seasonal shelving to same-month comparisons across years, and a quiet pre-tour period to drawing silently in company.

Both explain why footwear matters to trouser length, why multiple changes need more time, and why one delay contact helps the team fill a gap. Both use a visible clock to pace the fitting, have the note taker confirm alterations while the costume is on, and record agreed sewing priorities when time is short.

Both move demonstrations away from live games, use a door-facing sign to welcome an opponent, and let visitors sit and read via a written queue when busy. Both settle takebacks before play, give lengthy analysis space away from quiet boards, and channel a rules disagreement privately to the host.
